history.dynasty: Late medieval period (temple architecture per jainstavan.in); 2014: 31-ft monolithic Vasupujya statue inaugurated at the Nathnagar complex
history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: this is a Jain temple; tradition set to Jainism. Keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. FLAG - CSV town wrong: the temple is at Champapur/Champanagar, Nathnagar (Bhagalpur district), not Bhagalpur city proper. Champapuri is the ancient capital of the Anga janapada and is unique as the only 'Panch Kalyanak Kshetra' in the world - the site of all five kalyanaks (garbha, janma, tapa, gyan, moksha) of the 12th Tirthankara, Lord Vasupujya (per jainsamaj.org and jain.org.in). Both Shwetamber (Panchkalyanak Tirtha, Tanti Bazar Road) and Digamber (Siddha Kshetra Bada Mandir) complexes exist at the site. Wikipedia's Vasupujya article notes a colossal 31-ft (9.4 m) monolithic statue of Vasupujya inaugurated at the Nathnagar complex in 2014. Coordinates are for the Champapuri Jain temple complex (Kabirpur, Nathnagar - geocoded full-address match); the Shwetamber Panchkalyanak Tirtha is adjacent on Tanti Bazar Road.

name: Shri Champapuri Vasupujya Swami Jain Tirtha
town_description: Nathnagar is a locality on the outskirts of Bhagalpur at the site of ancient Champapuri, once capital of the Anga janapada and today the Jain Panch Kalyanak Kshetra of Lord Vasupujya.
tradition: Jainism (Shwetamber Panchkalyanak Tirtha; Digamber temples also at the site) - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.railway: Bhagalpur Junction Railway Station is the nearest major station (per jainstavan.in); the complex is a short drive from it.
travel.road: The city is well connected by road (per jainstavan.in); local buses and taxis reach Nathnagar/Champapur.
